# Dsql

**Parity grade: A** · SDK `aws-sdk-go-v2/service/dsql@v1.22.3` · last audited 2026-10-10 (`5bb0d02ee`)

### Known gaps

- Data plane opt-in (DSQL_ENGINE=docker, or --engines=auto/docker with a reachable runtime; default stub keeps the control plane only). The cluster endpoint <id>.dsql.<region>.on.aws is not resolvable and clients cannot assume port 5432: connect to host/port from GET /_gopherstack/dsql/clusters/{id}; tokens are generated for the control-plane endpoint (also accepted: endpoint:port, loopback:port). The CA is served at /_gopherstack/dsql/ca.pem.
- Cluster data is ephemeral: each data plane is a fresh postgres container with no volume, so a restart or snapshot restore re-creates clusters (CREATING until up) with an empty database.
- Not published (checked the troubleshooting, unsupported-features and authentication-authorization User Guide pages): the SQLSTATE of the login failure (28P01 used) and the text and SQLSTATE of unsupported-feature rejections (0A000 '<feature> is not supported in Aurora DSQL'; the guide gives only 'Error: Not supported') and the full text of the plain CREATE INDEX rejection (the guide titles it 'use CREATE INDEX ASYNC instead')
- Unsupported-feature rejection covers CREATE TRIGGER, temporary tables, TRUNCATE, VACUUM, CREATE TABLESPACE, CREATE DATABASE and LANGUAGE plpgsql functions at the statement start only (not inside multi-statement strings or DO blocks). Foreign keys and sequences are accepted: the current User Guide documents both as supported (the bd issue text predates that). Plain CREATE INDEX is rejected (ASYNC required). The unsupported set matches the migration guide (no triggers, temporary tables, TRUNCATE, VACUUM, tablespaces or extra databases; SQL functions but no PL/pgSQL).
- CREATE INDEX ASYNC runs a plain (blocking) CREATE INDEX in a background job: CONCURRENTLY deadlocks with a session in sys.wait_for_job, so a failed unique build leaves no INVALID index (DSQL leaves one). Old completed/failed rows are pruned on the next submit as documented; job_id is 26 base32 characters as in the docs, object_id is the index oid once built.
- Transaction rules are enforced inside PostgreSQL (event + statement triggers with transition tables), so they hold on both wire protocols: one DDL per transaction and no DDL/DML mixing (SQLSTATE 0A000), 3,000 rows per transaction across INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (54000 'transaction row limit exceeded', text from the Quotas page), Repeatable Read as the database default, plain CREATE INDEX rejected, connections closed after 1 hour. UNVERIFIED text/codes (recalled, not documented): the DDL/DML messages, the plain CREATE INDEX message 'unsupported mode. please use CREATE INDEX ASYNC' (0A000). Still open: SET TRANSACTION to another isolation level is accepted, the Quotas-page limits other than the 3,000 row cap are not enforced (10 MiB per transaction 'transaction size limit 10mb exceeded', 5 minutes 'transaction age limit of 300s exceeded', 24 indexes per table, 255 columns, 10 schemas, 1,000 tables, 5,000 views and sequences, 1 KiB keys, 2 MiB rows and 1 MiB columns, all SQLSTATE 54000 or 54011 with the texts of CHAP_quotas), user DROP TRIGGER on the internal guard triggers is not blocked, and the C collation is not enforced.
- The cluster resource policy (PutClusterPolicy) is not evaluated at connect time; only the caller's identity policies are, and only when IAM enforcement is on. AWS IAM GRANT/REVOKE and sys.iam_pg_role_mappings are modelled (roles are logged in with an engine-private password), other sys.* views are absent.
- The postgres TLS front proxy duplicates the framing and startup code in services/rds/engine_proxy.go; a shared pkgs/ package is a follow-up.

### Structural gaps

These do not block an A grade — no implementation could produce real data here because the underlying data source cannot exist in an emulator.

- bypassPolicyLockoutSafetyCheck (CreateCluster, PutClusterPolicy) is accepted but not evaluated: the lockout check asks whether the calling principal keeps access, and the emulator has no authenticated caller identity or IAM policy evaluation (same stance as services/kms).
- GetVpcEndpointServiceName returns wire-shaped names only: there is no PrivateLink / VPC endpoint plane to back them.
